Pastey 2.0 runs a native coding Agent on another of your own devices. From one device you start Codex on a paired device, follow the run, answer its approvals, stop it, and receive its reply, over a Bridge that both devices authenticate. Codex is the production Agent adapter in this release.

## What's new in 2.0

- **Cross-device native Agent execution.** Start Codex in a folder on another device, or continue an existing Codex thread there. The requesting device shows the run's progress, Codex's command and file-change approvals (Approve once or Deny), Stop, and Codex's final reply.
- **The executing device decides.** Every request from another device waits for Accept on the device that runs it, unless that device's user has given the requesting device Full Access.
- **Full Access** for unattended use. Given on the controlled device after a consent dialog, it lets one paired device start Codex runs and open a Developer Terminal there without anyone clicking Accept. It works in one direction only, lasts until revoked, and ends with Revoke, Forget, re-pairing or Burn.
- **Bridges across the internet** (off by default). Paired devices on different networks connect directly through NATs where the networks allow it, otherwise through a relay (n0's public relays, or your own).
- **Authenticated pairing and reconnect.** Devices pair once with a one-time code and then reconnect without one, each proving the identity key the other remembers.
- **Workspaces shared per Bridge**, with separate switches for reading sessions and accepting Agent requests, and read-only views of the Codex and Claude Code sessions on another device.
- **Workspace movement:** send a folder to another device, run Codex on it there, and bring the result back. It is applied only if your copy is unchanged; otherwise it is kept for you to review. See the known limitations below.
- A redesigned interface organised around Bridges, with Share and Agents tabs.

## Identity, authority and recovery

These rules are enforced in code and covered by automated tests, including deterministic two-device tests. Physical testing coverage is listed in the next section.

- **Identity.** The pairing code is the one-time password of a SPAKE2 exchange, so it cannot be recovered by listening. Each device pins the other's identity key. Reconnect requires proof of that key over fresh nonces. Addresses, names and codes never count as identity.
- **Authority.** Control messages between devices are encrypted, and checked for replay and rate before anything acts on them. Every Agent task belongs to exactly one owner: this device or one Bridge. A remote request runs only after the executing device's Accept, or under Full Access when the requesting device has proved its identity in the current session. Anything Full Access starts has the rights of the Pastey process and never more. Pastey never answers Codex's own approvals or questions by itself.
- **Recovery.** A dropped connection never re-runs or re-sends Agent work. When an outcome is uncertain, the task says so and offers Reconcile. A final status that did not arrive is re-sent a bounded number of times, and Reconcile recovers it after that. A workspace movement whose delivery is uncertain keeps your source, and a returned result never overwrites a folder that changed in the meantime.

## Verified on physical devices

Packaged builds were tested on a Mac (Apple Silicon) and a Windows 11 PC. The Mac was on a phone hotspot and the Windows PC on home Wi-Fi.

- A Bridge across separate networks through the internet carrier.
- Remote Codex execution on Windows, requested from the Mac.
- Host identity and the secure session.
- Full Access, with the Mac controlling the Windows PC unattended.
- Connection and Agent recovery after a network outage or reconnect.
- Developer Mode after its session ends or the Bridge reconnects.

## Known limitations

- **Workspace movement and its return** have not completed physical end-to-end acceptance. Automated tests cover them.
- A second workspace movement or return that starts while one is still sending is **refused, not queued**. Wait for the first to finish before starting another.
- **Throughput across the internet is low** in the tests so far: about 0.4 MB/s for Test connection over a phone hotspot. The cause is not yet established. Through n0's public relays, about 1 MiB/s was measured.
- **Codex is the only native Agent adapter** shipped. Claude Code sessions can be viewed from another device but continued only on their own device.
- **Workspace movement** carries at most 1,024 regular files. It refuses symlinks, special files, empty folders, executable modes, names that collide when case is ignored, and names that are not portable between macOS and Windows.
- **Not verified physically:** remote session reading, relay-only connections, sleep and wake, and Full Access while Windows is locked.

## Platforms and prerequisites

| Platform | Download | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| macOS, Apple Silicon | `pastey_2.0.0_aarch64.dmg` | Tested on current macOS. No Intel build. |
| Windows 11 x64 | `pastey_2.0.0_x64-setup.exe` | Installs for the current user. Used in physical testing. |
| Windows 11 x64 | `pastey_2.0.0_x64_en-US.msi` | Installs for all users. Not used in physical testing. |

Linux is not tested or supported in 2.0.0.

To run Agents across devices:

- Install 2.0.0 on both devices and pair them once by code on the same network.
- On the device that runs Codex, install Codex and sign in, either the Codex CLI or the ChatGPT desktop app with its bundled Codex. Continuing an existing thread needs Codex 0.163.0-alpha.10.2 or later.
- To connect across networks, turn on Settings → General → Across the internet on both devices.
- For unattended use of a Windows PC, add Pastey to the Windows Startup folder. It has no background service.

## Install and upgrade

These builds are not code-signed or notarized.

- **macOS:** open the DMG and drag Pastey to Applications. If macOS blocks the first open, choose System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. If it says the app is damaged, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/pastey.app` once.
- **Windows:** run the installer. If SmartScreen says it protected your PC, choose More info → Run anyway.

When upgrading from 1.x or a 2.0 beta:

- Install over the existing app with the same kind of installer; on Windows, don't mix the `.exe` and `.msi`.
- Update both devices. Earlier versions cannot pair with or reconnect to 2.0.0.
- A Bridge from an earlier version stays disconnected, with its content kept, until you pair it again from its network panel.
- Unattended Codex permissions from earlier builds are removed. Give Full Access on the controlled device instead.

The full list of changes is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/xpan0988/Pastey/blob/v2.0.0/CHANGELOG.md).
